title: STEREO FEEDBACK DELAY -- mono-in, stereo-out tape-style echo

sections.heading: USING IT
lines: Turn on audio with the speaker button. Input is mic/line input 1.
mono in slider: input level, with its meter beside it.
Time: delay time, 1-2000 ms. Changing it glides the pitch like tape.
Feedback: how much of each echo repeats (up to 95%, so it always dies away).
Damp: cutoff of the filter inside the loop. Lower = darker repeats.
Rate / Depth: speed and amount of the slow tape warble.
Drive: soft saturation inside the loop. More drive = grittier, quieter repeats.
Width: offset of the right channel (0-30 ms) for stereo width.
stereo out sliders: output level for left and right.
Presets 1-6: Slapback, Dub Echo, Tape Wobble, Wide Ambience, Long Trails, Clean Digital.
Shift-click a preset bubble to store the current dials. Gain sliders are not stored.

sections.heading: HOW IT WORKS
lines: One gen~ codebox holds a single delay line (up to 2 s) with a smoothed, interpolated read.
The loop runs: read > lowpass > soft clip > feedback amount > back into the line.
The right channel is a second read slightly later than the left, outside the loop.
